history.summary: Radha Krishna Mandir, popularly Jalan Mandir, is a well-known Krishna temple in Jalan Nagar, Dibrugarh, just outside the Assam Medical College campus. It was established by the Jalan family, prominent tea planters and entrepreneurs of Upper Assam, after whom the Jalan Nagar locality is named. The complex holds subsidiary shrines to Shiva, Rani Sati and Hanuman alongside the main Radha-Krishna sanctum. The building uses white marble with Marwari/Rajasthani influence in a Nagara layout, the main shrine on the first floor. Janmashtami and Jhulan Yatra (idols placed on a decorated swing) are the main festivals. The temple is ~1.8 km from Dibrugarh railway station per Wikipedia (verify). Opening hours conflict across sources - verify locally.

town_description: Dibrugarh is Upper Assam's 'Tea City', the headquarters of Dibrugarh district on the south bank of the Brahmaputra, about 50 km southwest of Tinsukia. It hosts Assam Medical College and Dibrugarh University, and the Bogibeel rail-cum-road bridge; it is a gateway to Arunachal Pradesh.
